headline: Taiwan's economics minister says the island plans to add advanced AI chips and AI servers to its export control list, with criminal charges possible for unauthorised shipments to China.
score_reason: Lowered from 8 to 7: the pool headline said 'strict controls' but the minister described a plan with no start date or product list.
importance_line: It would give prosecutors a clearer legal basis against AI hardware smuggling to China, which matters to exporters, server makers and Washington, since the step is part of Taiwan's trade deal with the US, but there is no start date and no list of covered products yet.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Taiwan News, that Economics Minister Kung Ming-hsin said Taiwan plans to add advanced semiconductors and AI servers to its export control list under its trade agreement with the United States, so that unauthorised shipments could bring criminal charges under the Foreign Trade Act. He gave no start date, and Taiwan's Central News Agency notes that current permit rules do not specifically cover AI chips and servers, which has made some smuggling cases hard to prosecute.
notes: Read via Taiwan News (taiwannews.com.tw/news/6459737), which relays the Bloomberg interview; the Bloomberg link is the original (decoded from Google News, not opened). Day of the interview unclear (Taiwan News says Monday, Bloomberg published Friday 16 Oct 2026).
